summary: Created an SSH host CA on node1, signed the host's ed25519 key into a certificate, configured sshd to present it, and verified a client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) connects without prompting. Then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id/service health, issued a native reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd health and the CA-based trust behavior post-restart.
actions_performed: Generated an ed25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca on node1
Signed node1's existing ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub with the CA into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals: node1, node IP, localhost; valid forever)
Added 'HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config, validated with sshd -t, and restarted the sshd service to apply it
Built a known_hosts file containing only an @cert-authority line for the CA public key (no pinned host key) and confirmed ssh connects and verifies the host via the certificate
Sanity-checked that a client with neither CA trust nor a pinned key fails host key verification, isolating the CA as the source of trust

Captured pre-restart boot_id and sshd/cert health, issued a native reboot on node1 whose acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled until exec access returned, and confirmed the boot_id changed
Re-verified post-restart sshd status, the effective HostCertificate config, cert validity, and the CA-trust-only connection test

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline: sshd healthy, host cert configured and active
evidence.summary: sshd -t passed, service restarted/started, and sshd -T showed hostcertificate active before the node restart; boot_id 272eff4c-5c0e-4adb-8653-6b4d70d5e553 recorded as baseline.

evidence.requirement: CA created and host certificate correctly signed
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated the CA at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca and signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub into ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1, 10.100.115.10, localhost, valid forever; ssh-keygen -L confirmed the cert structure and signing CA fingerprint.

evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) connects without host-key prompting
evidence.summary: With UserKnownHostsFile containing only an @cert-authority entry for the CA pubkey, ssh -vv showed 'Host key verification... is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' and proceeded to auth (Permission denied on pubkey/password, i.e. host verification succeeded); a client with neither CA trust nor a pinned key instead got 'Host key verification failed', isolating the CA as the trust source.
`sudo -n reboot` was launched via nohup/disown in the background and the exec call returned 'reboot_issued' successfully before the connection dropped on the next poll.

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Repeated polling after issuing the reboot showed connection resets/timeouts (node down/rebooting), then exec access returned with boot_id f9af7005-7ab3-485c-b97e-097a8812e2e1, differing from the pre-restart boot_id 272eff4c-5c0e-4adb-8653-6b4d70d5e553, proving an actual OS restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sshd, host certificate config, and CA-based trust behavior
evidence.summary: After the restart, rc-service sshd status showed 'started', sshd -T still listed the HostCertificate path, ssh-keygen -L re-confirmed the cert, and the CA-only known_hosts client test again showed 'is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate' followed by auth-stage denial, proving the certificate-based trust setup survived and functions after the restart.
